observation.visible_scene: A stainless steel saucepan, its handle angled toward the upper right, sits on a gas stovetop viewed from a high angle. The pan is filled with clear water containing many floating ice cubes of varying sizes clustered across the surface. Black stove grate bars frame the pan, a speckled granite counter is visible at the left edge, and white control knobs appear at the lower right. The framing and lighting stay constant throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The overall layout of the pan, water, and ice cubes remains essentially unchanged from the first to the last sampled frame; no ice cube visibly translates, rotates, or rearranges in a way distinguishable across the segment.
No visible boiling, bubbling, or rapid melting is apparent at this timescale; the water surface and ice edges look static.

A small circular highlight (a bubble or surface reflection) on the right side of the ice cluster becomes noticeable around the middle of the excerpt and persists to the end, while the surrounding ice stays in place.
The camera viewpoint and the positions of the stove grate, counter, and knobs do not shift, indicating a fixed camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the burner is lit or heating the pan is not shown.
Any actual melting rate or eventual disappearance of the ice is outside this short segment.
The cause of the small mid-clip surface highlight (rising bubble vs. shifting reflection) is not determinable here.
uncertain_details: Possible sub-pixel drift of individual ice cubes due to convection cannot be confirmed from these frames.
The small right-side circle could be a bubble, a reflection, or a slight change in ice shape; its nature is ambiguous.
Whether the water level changed by a tiny amount is not reliably visible.
